Where it began

Corbin Bosch was born in Durban on 10 September 1994, the son of the former South African cricketer Tertius Bosch. He came through the junior ranks quickly and was part of the South Africa side that won the Under-19 World Cup in 2014.

His senior career began with Titans, first in T20 cricket in November 2014 and then in first-class cricket in September 2017. He also played for Northerns and, in time, for franchise teams around the world, from Rajasthan Royals and Barbados Royals to Paarl Royals and Mumbai Indians.

The player

His call to the Test side came in December 2024, for the series against Pakistan, and he made his debut at Centurion on Boxing Day. His very first ball accounted for the Pakistan captain, Shan Masood, making him the fifth South African to take a wicket with his first delivery in Tests. He went on to take four for 63.

Then he batted. Coming in at number nine with South Africa 191 for seven and behind on the first innings, he hit an unbeaten 81 from 93 balls, with 15 fours, and turned a deficit into a lead of 90. It was then the highest score by a number nine on Test debut, and no South African had made a fifty and taken four wickets in his first Test. In June 2025 he made his first Test hundred, against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo.

What made him special

He showed himself the kind of all-rounder captains love: a bowler who can break a stand and a middle-order batsman who stays calm when the score looks thin. In his first four Tests he made 245 runs at 61.25 with a top score of 100 not out, and took 16 wickets at 18.88, with a best of five for 43.

His one-day debut, a few days before his first Test, told the same story. He dismissed the centurion Saim Ayub and then made 40 from 44 balls from number eight. If there is a weakness, it is that he kept arriving with the team in trouble, which rather spoils the quiet afternoon he might have hoped for.

Away from the middle

Bosch has carried his game around the world, from the Caribbean Premier League to the SA20. In May 2022 he joined Rajasthan Royals in the IPL as a replacement for Nathan Coulter-Nile, and in 2025 he joined Mumbai Indians. He also toured Sri Lanka with South Africa A in 2023.

And finally

Most debutants spend their first Test hoping not to be noticed. Bosch took a wicket before he had time to settle his nerves, then made a record score down the order. It set a high bar for the second Test.
